Accra De Morue

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 15 min

Accra De Morue are traditional Haitian salt cod fritters commonly served during Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa. This festival honors the spirit of agriculture and harvest, and these crispy, savory fritters symbolize abundance and the fruits of the land and sea.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup dried salted cod (about 150g)
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour (120g)
  • 1/2 cup water (120ml)
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 small Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and finely chopped
  • 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
  • Vegetable oil for frying

Method

  1. Rinse the dried salted cod under cold water to remove excess salt and soak it in water for 4 to 6 hours, changing the water once or twice.
  2. Drain the cod and place it in a pot with fresh water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes until tender. Drain and let cool.
  3. Remove any bones and skin from the cod, then flake the fish into small pieces.
  4. In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, salt, and black pepper.
  5. Add the water gradually, stirring to create a thick batter.
  6. Mix in the flaked cod, chopped onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet pepper, and parsley until well combined.
  7. Heat about 2 inches (5 cm) of vegetable oil in a deep skillet or pot over medium heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C).
  8. Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding.
  9. Fry each batch for about 3 to 4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
  10. Use a slotted spoon to remove the fritters and drain them on paper towels.
  11. Serve hot as a festive appetizer or snack during the Fete de Papa Zaka.

Tips

  • Adjust the heat of the Scotch bonnet pepper to your preference or substitute with a milder chili for less spice.
  • For extra flavor, add a splash of lime juice or finely chopped scallions to the batter.
  • Serve with a spicy dipping sauce or pikliz (Haitian pickled vegetables) for an authentic experience.
